message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Category | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |----------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds part of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.). | • Report problems in writing (email or letter).
• If the landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent, repair and deduct, or file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable (usually not more than 5% of the rent). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter the unit without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hrs) except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any unannounced entries. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect your privacy; they cannot conduct searches without a warrant or court order unless you consent. | • If you suspect a warrantless search, document the incident and consider contacting a lawyer. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a lease with proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month).
• Landlord must provide a written notice of termination. | • Keep copies of all notices. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, provided you follow the proper procedure. | • Document the problem, send a written notice, keep receipts, and give the landlord a chance to fix it before deducting. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Eviction must go through the court; the landlord cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond to notices promptly; if you believe the eviction is unlawful, file a defense in court. | | **Maintenance of Records** | • Landlord must keep records of rent payments and maintenance requests. | • Request copies if needed for disputes. | | **Legal Remedies** | • You can sue for damages, recover unpaid rent, or seek injunctive relief if the landlord violates your rights. | • Small claims court is available for disputes under $10,000. | ### Quick Steps If You Encounter Problems 1. **Document Everything** – Keep written records, photos, and receipts. 2. **Communicate in Writing** – Send emails or certified mail to the landlord. 3. **Know the Notice Periods** – Texas law specifies how much notice is required for entry, repairs, and termination. 4. **Seek Mediation** – Many cities offer free or low‑cost mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes. 5. **File a Complaint** – If the landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with TDHCA, TCHR, or HUD. 6. **Consult an Attorney** – For complex issues (e.g., eviction, discrimination), a lawyer can help protect your interests. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** | Information on tenant rights, landlord responsibilities, and how to file complaints. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** | Handles discrimination complaints. | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | Federal fair housing resources. | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | Free legal clinics, mediation, and advocacy. | | **Texas Property Code** | The statutory law governing landlord‑tenant relationships. | Feel free to ask if you need more detail on any specific right or how to handle a particular situation!
